Conflict: In-Service Agent recommends high-impact virgin ABS/PC for durability and impact resistance, while Circularity Agent and Material and Design Agent recommend monomaterial PCR-PP to maximize recycled content and end-of-life recyclability.
Agents Involved: In-Service Agent; Circularity Agent; Material and Design Agent
Decision: Monomaterial post-consumer recycled polypropylene (PCR-PP) without overmolding
Rationale: Using PCR-PP aligns with sustainability best practices by maximizing recycled content and ensuring high-quality mechanical recycling at end-of-life. Durability concerns can be addressed through mechanical design optimizations, such as internal ribbing, rather than relying on carbon-intensive virgin plastics.
ESPR Citation: Lifecycle principle: material durability vs. end-of-life recyclability

Conflict: Manufacture Agent recommends ultrasonic welding to minimize assembly time and part count, whereas Circularity Agent and In-Service Agent recommend reversible mechanical fasteners to enable non-destructive disassembly for repair and recycling.
Agents Involved: Manufacture Agent; Circularity Agent; In-Service Agent
Decision: Reversible mechanical fasteners (standardized screws and snap-fits)
Rationale: Reversible fasteners are selected because they enable non-destructive disassembly, facilitating repair, component reuse, and clean material separation at end-of-life, which provides a significantly lower overall lifecycle environmental impact than permanent ultrasonic welds.
ESPR Citation: Lifecycle principle: manufacturing simplicity vs. ease of disassembly and repair

Conflict: In-Service Agent recommends a high-efficiency BLDC motor with rare-earth magnets for superior energy efficiency, whereas Material and Design Agent and Manufacture Agent recommend rare-earth-free motors to avoid critical raw materials and toxic extraction impacts.
Agents Involved: In-Service Agent; Material and Design Agent; Manufacture Agent
Decision: High-efficiency BLDC motor designed for non-destructive magnet and bearing extraction
Rationale: This option balances the high operational energy efficiency required during the use phase with a circular design that allows clean recovery of rare-earth magnets at end-of-life, satisfying both resource conservation and energy efficiency goals.
ESPR Citation: Lifecycle principle: operational energy efficiency vs. critical raw material recovery

Conflict: In-Service Agent recommends a dedicated filtered auxiliary cooling fan to prevent motor burnout, while Material and Design Agent and Manufacture Agent recommend passive cooling via integrated airflow channels to minimize weight, material use, and assembly complexity.
Agents Involved: In-Service Agent; Material and Design Agent; Manufacture Agent
Decision: Passive cooling via optimized airflow channels and detachable aluminum heatsinks
Rationale: Passive cooling avoids the manufacturing footprint, added weight, and electronic waste of an auxiliary motor and fan. Thermal reliability can be managed via simple thermal cut-off switches and optimized venting geometry.
ESPR Citation: Lifecycle principle: active component reliability vs. material minimization

Conflict: Manufacture Agent recommends a monolithic integrated design to simplify assembly and reduce production waste, whereas Circularity Agent and In-Service Agent recommend a modular architecture to facilitate repair and component reuse.
Agents Involved: Manufacture Agent; Circularity Agent; In-Service Agent
Decision: Modular cartridge design with easily separable functional blocks
Rationale: A modular architecture prevents premature product disposal when a single component fails, which outweighs the minor manufacturing simplicity of a monolithic design by significantly extending the product's active service life.
ESPR Citation: Lifecycle principle: manufacturing waste reduction vs. product life extension

Conflict: Circularity Agent recommends a removable, modular Li-ion battery pack to ensure cordless convenience and battery circularity, whereas Material and Design Agent, Manufacture Agent, and In-Service Agent recommend corded AC power to eliminate battery degradation and hazardous materials.
Agents Involved: Circularity Agent; Material and Design Agent; Manufacture Agent; In-Service Agent
Decision: Corded AC power supply with integrated cable reel
Rationale: Corded AC power completely eliminates the environmental impact of battery manufacturing, avoids hazardous substances of concern (lithium, cobalt, nickel), and prevents premature product obsolescence due to battery degradation.
ESPR Citation: Lifecycle principle: cordless user convenience vs. battery-induced environmental footprint
